status: Closed — canonical planning-root preference and missing-root diagnostics verified 2026-09-05
area: Default planning-root resolution prefers a non-existent root over the canonical root named by the cards' own creation seals
finding: Planning commands resolve a default planning root from configuration and environment without confirming that the resolved location exists or holds a series registry. When the resolved directory is absent, the failure is reported as an unregistered series rather than as an unresolvable root, and the suggested recovery is to register a series that is in fact already registered under owner approval in the real root. Two consequences follow. An operator acting on the suggestion would create a duplicate series and a second planning authority for ids that already exist, which is exactly what the no-new-series rule forbids; and the true defect, a root that does not resolve, is never named, so the same misdiagnosis repeats for every command that touches planning.
expectedBehavior: Root resolution must fail closed on its own terms. A configured or inherited planning root that does not exist, or that exists without a series registry, must produce a distinct error naming the path it tried, why it was rejected, and which candidate roots were considered. Registry-derived facts already present in the repository outrank an unverified default: task cards carry a planning creation seal recording the root they were authored under, and that recorded root should be preferred, or at minimum offered, before any suggestion to create new planning structure. No recovery hint may propose registering a series without first checking whether that series is already registered in a reachable root.
evidenceOrRepro: Original reproduction on 2026-08-16: a missing configured planning root was misreported as an unregistered GOV series and suggested duplicate registration. The repair landed in f43c3c9e9499149f282c4b76eac27fab5799ae73.
